answer: A Sybil attack dies at the cost gate. Each agent identity must post an economic bond keyed to a hardware attestation, so running ten thousand puppet identities means ten thousand bonds, not one. The protocol samples a random anchor set of bonded agents per epoch; their independent signal votes on transaction validity, and a bond is slashed when its holder signs a fork. Because attestation binds identity to a scarce device and the bond is forfeited on proven misbehaviour, each fake island of identities costs a real stake plus the risk of total loss, making mass identity creation unprofitable.
